Who it's for

Families who already own their curriculum and are tired of turning teacher manuals into a daily plan, especially with more than one child on different programs. It doesn't sell curriculum or push a method; it organises the one you chose.

What OneHomeschool does

🗓️

Daily lesson guides

Which lessons are review and which introduce new concepts, every assignment and test, and the pages to open.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦

Every child on one screen

What's done, what's left and how the week is pacing, for each child. Jump to any date.

📈

Progress with finish dates

Each subject shows when the book was meant to finish and when it actually will at the current pace.

🎓

Attendance & transcripts

Attendance counts as lessons are checked off; grades become transcripts with GPA and credits, as PDF or CSV.

✍️

On-screen assessments

Generated from the lessons and graded instantly on screen, saved to the progress history.

🧒

A kids' view

Touchscreen-friendly; students check off their own work. Chores can sit alongside schoolwork.

📱

Apps & calendar sync

iOS and Android apps, and sync with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Skylight and DAKboard.

🖨️

Paper when you want it

The day prints on one sheet per child. The school calendar imports US holidays in one click.

Does it work with my curriculum?

OneHomeschool works alongside the books you already own. The supported list grows every week, so the official curriculum page is the only reliable answer; any list in an article (including this one) goes out of date. "One curriculum" there means a complete program across every grade it covers.

Check the supported curriculum list ↗

Good fit, or not quite?

Likely a good fit

  • You already own your curriculum and want the daily plan done for you
  • You teach two or more children on different programs or paces
  • You want attendance and transcripts kept as you go
  • Your kids are ready to check off their own work

Maybe not

  • You want a tool that sells or chooses a curriculum for you
  • Your main programs aren't on the supported list yet
  • You need it to decide whether you meet your state's rules; that's between you and your state

How to try it

  1. Check your curriculum on the official list.
  2. Start the 14-day trial, with no card needed, and add each child.
  3. Run a real week: open the daily guide each morning and let the kids use their view.
  4. If it fits, pick a plan and use code GIORGI2608 for 5% off your first payment.

OneHomeschool FAQ

How much does OneHomeschool cost?
Starter is $99/year or $12.99/month for up to 2 students. Family is $149/year or $19.99/month for up to 4. Complete is $199/year or $24.99/month for up to 8.
Is there a free trial?
Yes. Every plan starts with a 14-day free trial of the full platform, no credit card, plus a 14-day money-back guarantee.
Does it sell curriculum?
No. It works alongside the curriculum you already own and doesn't push a teaching method.
Does it support my curriculum?
Check the official curriculum page. The list changes every week.
Can an ESA or scholarship pay for it?
Many states have programs that can cover educational software, and OneHomeschool provides itemised per-student invoices. Check your state's program for eligibility.
Who built it?
A homeschooling family of five with three kids on three different curricula. They built it for their own mornings.
